children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

Since Alex is 18 years old, they fall into the 16-19 age category where eligibility depends on their current situation.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A traineeship in England
- Home education (if started before they turned 18)

Or has Alex perhaps registered with a careers service or the armed services after leaving education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school and aren't doing A-levels or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex is 18 and not in approved education or training, I have a couple more questions to determine if there might still be eligibility:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

If a 16 or 17 year old registers with one of these services, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks – but since Alex is 18, this wouldn't apply unless they registered when they were 16 or 17.

Also, just to confirm:

**Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more a week, or receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. And no, they're not working - certainly not anything like 24 hours a week. They're just at home at the moment, and they're not getting any benefits in their own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all those details.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, I need to share some disappointing news about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

To summarise Alex's situation:
- Alex is 18 years old
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex did not register with a careers service or armed services when they were 16 or 17
- Alex is not working 24+ hours a week or receiving benefits in their own right

**The key issue is that Child Benefit for children aged 16-19 normally only continues if the child stays in approved education or training.** Since Alex is 18 and not in any approved education or training, and didn't register with a careers service or armed services at 16 or 17 (which would have allowed a 20-week extension), there is no basis for eligibility.

Let me now provide you with my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Summary

| Child | Age | Eligible? |
|-------|-----|-----------|
| Alex | 18 | No |

### Reason

Child Benefit for children aged 16 and over is normally only available if the child stays in **approved education or training** until they turn 20. Since Alex is 18, has finished school, and is not in any approved education or training, you would not qualify.

The option to extend Child Benefit for 20 weeks by registering with a careers service or the armed services is only available to 16 or 17 year olds when they leave education – so this doesn't apply to Alex now that they're 18.

### What could change this?

If Alex were to enrol in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs up to Level 3, or other qualifying courses), you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for them again, provided they start before turning 19. If this happens, you could make a new claim at that time.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
